title: Grown-Ups Race Wacky Homemade Cars Down a Volcano in Portland!
summary:
Have you ever built a car out of junk and raced it downhill? In Portland, Oregon, grown-ups do that every year at the Adult Soap Box Derby. It just celebrated its 27th year! This race is not about being the fastest. It's about being the most creative and having fun.

On August 15, 42 cars lined up at Mt. Tabor Park. Mt. Tabor is actually an old volcano! The cars were amazing. One looked like a giant sloth head. Another was a Zamboni from a hockey show. There was a car like the Flintstones' car, and one that looked like a famous dead whale from Oregon. John Nurse built a dragon car because his 10-year-old kid drew a picture of one. He used hula hoops and foam to make it. "How many times do you get to race a dragon down a volcano?" he asked.

Soap box derbies started a long time ago. Kids used to race in them. But in Portland, it's for adults who want to act like kids again. The cars have to have brakes and helmets, but anything else goes. Some cars are covered in fake fur or shiny tiles.

Thousands of people came to watch. They brought chairs and blankets and cheered for hours. Brittany England made an ice cream truck car called the Rocky Roadster. She said, "The vibes are great, the energy's awesome." The derby president, David Paulsen, called it "a party that Portland throws for itself." He first saw it in 1997 and loved it right away. He said the cars are like "booger-welded garbage cars racing down a mountain." That sounds gross, but also really fun!
why_it_matters: Events like this remind us that playfulness and creativity can bring a whole community together, just like a school art fair or field day.
